questions.question: What is the approved physical ordering and side allocation of the return-branch valve groups relative to pumps P1 and P2: specifically, which of V18, V23, V22, V1, V3 are suction-side versus discharge-side around P1, and which of V20, V24, V25, V5, V6 are suction-side versus discharge-side around P2?
questions.reasoning: The brief authoritatively resolves branch destinations and valve-group membership by function, but explicitly says the exact internal ordering and which subset is suction-side versus discharge-side is not fully established. That affects detailed hydraulic topology, static head, and isolation logic.
questions.suggested_value: For the immediately usable benchmark topology, keep the pumps adjacent to their source tanks and place each listed valve group downstream in the listed order: B7 -> P1 -> V18 -> V23 -> V22 -> V1 -> V3 -> B2, and B6 -> P2 -> V20 -> V24 -> V25 -> V5 -> V6 -> B1.
options: All listed branch valves downstream of the pump in the listed order
Some valves upstream and some downstream per final P&ID
Valve-group order different from the listed sequence but branch membership unchanged

questions.question: How should NaCl composition targets be represented in the mandatory StandardWater benchmark acceptance model?
questions.reasoning: The brief requires StandardWater as the authoritative acceptance medium for topology validation, but also requires demonstration of B3 and B5 NaCl mass-fraction targets. StandardWater alone cannot supply composition-dependent NaCl states, so a representation choice materially affects whether QI-302 and QIS-502 are modeled as real state-based measurements versus placeholders.
questions.suggested_value: Use StandardWater for hydraulic and thermal medium properties, plus a parallel surrogate scalar NaCl mass-fraction state propagated by constituent mass conservation in B3 and B5 for benchmark acceptance checks; reserve full WaterNaCl thermophysical coupling for a higher-fidelity variant.
options: StandardWater plus surrogate scalar NaCl state
WaterNaCl-only for composition demonstrations in a separate model
Custom wrapper medium combining StandardWater hydraulics with scalar composition tracking

questions.question: What is the approved guard logic for opening and closing V15 during the post-evaporation transfer from B5 to B7?
questions.reasoning: The brief clearly identifies V15 as the B5-to-B7 discharge valve and uses V15 closed as part of the B5-idle interlock, but it also states that the exact guard for opening and closing V15 is not fully established from the notes. That materially affects the discrete sequence in the parallel branch.
questions.suggested_value: Open V15 immediately after evaporation completion when the sequence enters the post-evaporation branch, and close V15 when B5 reaches its practical empty/idle threshold LIS_501 <= 0.01 m before or at branch completion to B7 cooling/return.
options: Open at evaporation complete; close at LIS_501 <= 0.01 m
Open at evaporation complete; close when B7 high target is reached
Different explicit sequence guard from final approved controller

status: compiles and passes real omc simulate() over the full declared 0-3000s acceptance window
gap: Real trajectory verification (compile_files with result_csv_path, not just the compiler PASS status) shows the batch does NOT complete the full described cycle within the 3000s window. mode reaches Step6_Heat_and_Evaporate_B5 and stays there through t=3000s; QIS_502 (B5 NaCl mass fraction) reaches only ~0.151 against the required 0.180 target, so the mode never advances to JoinWait, the parallel branchA/branchB dispatch (B6/B7 cooling and return routing) never fires, and the cycle-restart at t>2500s never occurs. Everything upstream of Step6 (B3 prefill/concentration/transfer, B5 charge, all interlocks) verified correct against the merged understanding.
root_cause: The merged understanding gives B5 heater duty (20000 W), charge level (0.18 m), evaporation target (0.180 kg/kg), and a fixed acceptance StopTime (3000 s) with restart gate (time > 2500 s), but never states B5 cross-sectional area. Stage 3 must derive that area itself; across 9 real fix-and-rerun cycles (each independently verified via real omc simulate() + real CSV trajectory inspection, never hand-patched) it converged steadily -- QIS_502 reached 0, then 0.089, then 0.115, then 0.151 -- but has not yet landed on an area small enough to finish evaporation with margin inside the declared window.
fixed_this_session: cross-when-block live discrete reference cycles (two state machines reading each others live value instead of pre(), causing repeated purely-discrete-algebraic-loop compile failures)
a fabricated evaporation-rate penalty formula that stayed at exactly 0.0 for the entire simulation
immediate-pass-through stalls (an exit condition already true on state entry, with no future event to catch it, silently stalling ~1900-2000s until an unrelated timer forced re-evaluation)
unstated vessel area silently defaulted to 1.0 sq m instead of being derived from the briefs own rate and timing evidence
decision: User explicitly chose to accept the current compiling-but-incomplete result and document this gap rather than continue iterating further this session. All prompt fixes above are permanent (in src/simulation_platform/skills/stage3_modelica.py) and benefit any future rerun of this or other projects. No files were hand-patched at any point -- every fix went through the pipelines own execute_reasoner_stage_3 repair loop against the real compiler.
